clue.text: TV presenter is given a new job that's dull mostly

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a dull task is a chore

explanation.surface: A television presenter gets landed with a tedious new role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter from CHORE, leaving CHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A news anchor is the presenter who fronts a television programme.

clue.text: Mountain height, a risk for several characters

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
a bet is a risk taken

explanation.surface: Climbing a high peak is a gamble for a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabet is a set of letters, i.e. many written characters.

clue.text: One may take the heat out of the situation

definitions.text: One may take the heat out of the situation

parts.words: One may take the heat out of the situation
parts.note: read as calming a tense moment, but literally a fluid that draws off heat from an engine

explanation.surface: Someone who can calm down a tense moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A coolant is a liquid that carries heat away from machinery.

clue.text: Arrangement with bank manager finally accepted by maiden? Silly!

parts.note: a maiden over in cricket is an over with no runs

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the silly word

parts.note: daft means silly

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of manager

explanation.surface: A naive young woman foolishly agrees a deal with her bank manager.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden is a cricket over in which no runs are scored; 'accepted by' puts R inside DAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is an arrangement letting a customer borrow from the bank beyond their balance.

clue.text: Wine or tot knocked back by trainee

indicators.note: by means next to, so the trainee follows
knocked back suggests a drink downed, but here it means the word is turned around

parts.note: to tot up is to add, giving a sum
a cadet is a trainee in the forces or police

explanation.surface: A choice between a glass of wine or a tot downed by a young recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns SUM into MUS; 'tot' looks like a small drink, but it is a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire valley.

clue.text: Government official needing to sort out nerdy creatures

indicators.note: to sort out means put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A civil servant who has to deal with geeky types.
explanation.definitionFit: An under-secretary is a junior minister or senior civil servant in government.

clue.text: Sounds like it's not goin' to be a plant

indicators.note: sounds like says the word is said aloud

parts.note: the opposite of going, in dropped-g speech, is comin'

explanation.surface: Someone saying they won't be going anywhere, like a rooted plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is a plant of the parsley family grown for its seeds.

clue.text: Daughter is young girl showing fire

parts.note: a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A daughter, still a young girl, displays a fiery temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning sack.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone is to sack them, to dismiss them from a job.

clue.text: Become nervous initially when trapped by nasty tutor

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside the anagram
nasty signals the letters of tutor are mangled
initially picks the first letter of nervous

explanation.surface: A jittery pupil cornered by an unpleasant teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges TUTOR into TUTRO; 'when trapped by' puts the N from 'nervous initially' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn to is to become, as water turns to ice.

clue.text: Pair in church marching around — he the ideal groom?

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A couple walking in procession through a church to meet the perfect husband.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England; 'around' signals an anagram of the word it follows, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Charming is the fairytale hero, the perfect man to marry.

clue.text: Religious individual before day's begun

parts.note: PI is short for pious, meaning religious
an individual is one
ere is a poetic word for before
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A devout person gets up before the day has started.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer something is to start it off first, so pioneered means begun or initiated.

clue.text: Bloke has no time for a meanie

indicators.note: has no says a letter is missing from the bloke's word

parts.note: a bloke is addressed as mister

explanation.surface: A man who never has time for a stingy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money, so is a meanie, a stingy person.

clue.text: Stop a group performing

parts.note: a band is a musical group
a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: A call to halt a group in the middle of their set.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a plan is to give it up, so to stop it.

clue.text: Became unrestrained in rave around port

indicators.note: around says the rave word wraps round the port

parts.note: to rave is to rant
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Someone let loose at a party held around a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is an idiom for behaving wildly, without restraint.

clue.text: Run as one of a crowd?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run not scored off the bat is an ...
a film ... is a member of a crowd scene

explanation.surface: Doubling as a background face in a crowd scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run given away by the fielding side, such as a wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a bonus run in cricket and a background actor in films.

clue.text: Set of problems with tax engaging lady of much wealth!

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the tax surrounds the lady

parts.note: excise is a duty or tax on goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, a very wealthy woman

explanation.surface: A list of maths problems about tax involving a rich woman.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina; the clue's 'lady of much wealth' is a playful description of her.
explanation.definitionFit: An exercise in a textbook is a set of problems for practice.

clue.text: Singer exciting his rector?

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A choirboy thrills the local vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a singer in a church choir.

clue.text: Playwright hinders a play

indicators.note: play looks like a drama, but here it means the letters move about

explanation.surface: A dramatist obstructs a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a drama, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was an Irish playwright, author of The Rivals.

clue.text: Yon American singer was once the No.2 female in UK?

parts.note: yon is an old word for that
Cher is a famous American singer

explanation.surface: A remote American singer was once Britain's second most important woman.
explanation.walkthrough: With the Queen as the first lady of the land, the woman who served as Prime Minister ranked second.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher, as Prime Minister, stood second only to the Queen among women in Britain.

clue.text: The fellow had to hug female relation? Spooky!

indicators.note: to hug means to wrap around, so the fellow surrounds the relative

parts.note: the fellow had contracts to he'd
an aunt is a female relation

explanation.surface: A man embracing his aunt finds it eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunted place is visited by ghosts, so spooky.

clue.text: Love having no speed at all? It brings zing!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
zero miles per hour, written O MPH

explanation.surface: Love without any pace still manages to bring excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is energy and vitality, much the same as zing.

clue.text: What's near top of agenda for at least 120 seconds?

definitions.meaning: the record of the last meeting is approved early in a meeting
two or more spans of sixty seconds

explanation.surface: An item early on the meeting's list will take a couple of minutes at least.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutes are the written record of a meeting and also plural units of sixty seconds.

clue.text: A loud blonde in extramarital relationship

parts.note: F is forte, the musical term for loud
fair hair is blonde

explanation.surface: A brash blonde caught in an illicit fling.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a romantic relationship outside a marriage.

clue.text: State of agitation in which female's left, say

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: A nervous moment when a woman is abandoned, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A flutter is a state of nervous excitement or agitation.

clue.text: Periods defined for school fees

definitions.meaning: the school year is divided into set periods
charges or prices asked, as in reasonable rates

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from one word: the divisions of the school year and the price or conditions offered.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms are the divisions of a school year and also the charges quoted for a service.

clue.text: Losing a bit finally, the inside becomes less bulky

indicators.note: losing its final bit means the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: the inside part is the inner

explanation.surface: Someone shedding weight at last, their middle becoming smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing a bit finally' drops the last letter of THE, giving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinner is the comparative of thin, so slimmer and less bulky.

clue.text: Sailor wants a litre on table

indicators.note: on here means put before, in this down-the-page sense of placing ahead

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor asks for a litre of drink to be put on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the table used in church for the Eucharist.

clue.text: Peevish or irate getting befouled with dirt

indicators.note: befouled means messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone already cross becomes angrier after being smeared with muck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befouled' rearranges the letters of IRATE and DIRT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritated means annoyed and peevish.

clue.text: Make new sketch for merchant ship's flag, omitting one of the names

indicators.note: omitting means one letter is dropped from the flag's name

parts.note: the Red Ensign is the flag of British merchant ships
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An artist redraws a merchant navy flag but leaves out a name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign is to draw up a new design, a fresh sketch.

clue.text: Publicity given to one boy in family creates stir

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, publicity
I is the Roman numeral one
a boy in a family is a son

explanation.surface: Media coverage of one of the family's boys causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' looks like a verb, but it is slang for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for jail, a place of confinement.
